records.summary: The 72E was the last form of Lotus's side-radiator, inboard-braked 72, reshaped for 1973 safety rules. The design won 20 Grands Prix and three constructors' titles between 1970 and 1975.
records.basis: Registered Wikipedia URL inspected: 72E from 1973 with bodywork for new safety regulations, constructors' titles 1970/1972/1973, 20 wins, retired after 1975.

records.summary: Lotus built the Elise GT1 for 1997 FIA GT after Porsche's 911 GT1 outgunned the Esprit GT1, making six race cars and one road car for homologation. It used the Esprit's 3.5-litre twin-turbo V8 or a Corvette LT5 V8.

records.summary: Ayrton Senna won twice and took eight poles in the 1986 98T, Lotus's last Renault turbo car, whose qualifying engines were credited with over 1,000 hp. Both five- and six-speed gearboxes ran that year.
records.basis: Registered Wikipedia URL inspected: two wins, eight poles, 1,000-1,200+ hp qualifying trim, final Renault season before Honda, five- and six-speed gearboxes. Keeps the existing gearbox-variation caveat in shorter form.

records.summary: The Lotus 25 brought the first fully stressed monocoque chassis to Formula One in 1962. Jim Clark won seven races and his first world title with it in 1963, using a Coventry Climax V8 and ZF five-speed.
records.basis: Wikipedia inspected: first fully stressed monocoque in F1, 1962 Dutch GP debut, Clark seven wins and 1963 title, Climax FWMV V8, ZF 5DS10.

records.basis: Registered Motor Sport article inspected: 10,000 rpm, more than 300 bhp, about 1500 rpm usable band, six-cylinder cars invariably quicker, project ended when Maserati gave up GP racing at end of 1957, five-speed transaxle.

records.summary: The 250F won first time out with Fangio in 1954, and in 1957 carried him to the title, including his Nurburgring comeback from 48 seconds down. Stirling Moss called it the best front-engined F1 car he drove.

open_questions: Record models a four-speed while the 1957 title car family moved to five speeds; summary avoids gear count.
